newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate flat, month-end pressures ease.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate flat, month-end pressures ease.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were unchanged at 22.00 in early trade on Tuesday, as month-end pressures in recent sessions eased, dealers said.
"We don't feel month-end pressures any more and speculation has halted. Everything looks stabler and conducive to a fall in secondary rates," a trader said.
One fixed-income analyst said rates had eased due to demand carried over from Monday, but they could come under pressure once more due to nervousness ahead of the July 6 mid-term elections.

"The nearer we get to the elections, the more pressure they will exert. The market has, however, practically ruled out hikes in U.S. interest rates," the analyst said, referring to the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on today and Wednesday.
"Buyers stepped in once (overnight Cetes) rates reached 25 percent on Monday, that is what controlled the escalation," he added.
Dealers said early strength in the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond, up 18/32 to yield 6.74 percent, had also helped keep Mexican rates stable.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile declined by 70 basis points
A liquidity shortfall of 715 million pesos was predicted due to prior central bank operations maturing.
